sections.h2: Offices that handle Knox County property tax
sections.html:
Two county offices share this job, and both sit inside the Knoxville City-County Building at 400 Main Street. Values and appeals belong to the Property Assessor at 865-215-2360. Payments belong to the Trustee in Suite 427 at 865-215-2305. Both open at eight and close at half past four on weekdays. A separate Assessor line, 865-215-2362, covers business personal property.

The Trustee's payment page lists six places to pay in person. Remote options:

  • Online, through the county's lookup tool; cards add a 2.5% fee and e-checks add $1.00
  • Phone: 865-215-2305, then option 3
  • Mail: P.O. Box 70, Knoxville, TN 37901

The Trustee's office also takes address changes online. The Assessor takes mailing address changes by phone at 865-215-2360.

sections.h2: Tax rate and how it is split
sections.html:
The fiscal 2026 levy is $1.5540 for each $100 of assessed value, and the County Commission sets it alongside the budget. Homes are assessed at 25% of appraised value, commercial property at 40%, and business personal property at 30%. The Assessor's FAQ gives the formula: appraised value, times the assessment percentage, times the combined city and county rate.

Living inside Knoxville means the city rate is added to the county one. The city's rate comes from the City of Knoxville, so call there for today's number.

The Assessor's calendar page lays out the tax year. Taxes for the current year come due on October 1. Pay by February 28 and there is no penalty or interest. A prior year's bill is delinquent from March 1.

The assessment side keeps its own schedule:

  • January 1 fixes ownership and condition for assessment purposes
  • March 15 is the last day to apply for greenbelt
  • May 20 is the exemption application cutoff, and change notices should be in the mail by then
  • June 1 opens the County Board of Equalization, which sits through the month
  • August 1 is the usual last day to reach the State Board, or 45 days after the county board's notice when that is later

Reappraisal here takes two years. The first is field work and sales data. The second applies the valuation models and mails new values along with appeal instructions. A higher value does not guarantee a higher bill, since the Commission may lower the rate afterward. Use the Assessor's calculator and parcel lookup to see where a value stands before the notice reaches you.

sections.h2: Tax relief and the senior freeze
sections.html:
Relief runs through the Trustee. For the 2026 senior freeze, an owner must turn 65 by December 31, 2026, and combined 2025 income for the owner, spouse and every deed owner must stay under $63,470, with VA income counted. Separate state relief reaches disabled-veteran owners, up to $444 for 2026 with no income limit, and the widows and widowers of a disabled veteran who have not remarried.

Applying early matters for a seller. If your relief credit is still pending when you list, tell the closing agent so the payoff and any credit are handled correctly at the table.

Think of relief as a state-funded credit toward payment instead of an exemption, so the bill still arrives and has to be paid. Enrollment for the 2026 tax year opens October 1, 2026 and closes April 5, 2027. The state fixes those dates, so the county cannot move them or grant extensions. Email applications are not accepted. You can request a form at taxrelief@knoxcounty.org or call the recorded information line at 865-215-8554.

The county counted 511,453 people on July 1, 2025, a 6.8% gain over April 2020. Owners occupy roughly 65.2% of homes, with a median value of $320,900. Median household income is $74,222. Typical monthly cost for an owner with a mortgage is $1,589, and typical rent is $1,261. Home values this high make an accurate assessment worth checking.

Knoxville is the county seat, and Farragut is in the county too. One Assessor and one Trustee serve all of it, so a Knoxville homeowner and a rural owner call the same numbers.

What this means when you sell: the tax bill follows the property, not the person, and the January 1 owner is on the roll. Before an offer is accepted, look up your parcel on the county lookup, see whether the current year is paid, and check whether earlier years show a balance. A clean record makes the title company's job simple, and a balance simply gets added to the payoff list. Call the Trustee at 865-215-2305 if the lookup shows something you do not recognize.

sections.h2: Selling a Knox County house with tax owed
sections.html:
Any change of ownership, even a private sale or a move into a trust or estate, prompts a sales questionnaire from the Assessor. The owner's name changes after the new deed is recorded with the Register of Deeds, a step that may take a week. Still seeing the old name a month later? Call 865-215-2360. The closing agent will get a payoff from the Trustee covering this year's bill plus any delinquent years.

Under Tennessee Code section 67-5-603, mid-year changes are prorated. A fire, a demolition or a completed addition between January 1 and September 1 alters the assessed value for just part of that year. Rebuilt or demolished something? Ask for a field review so the bill reflects the house you are actually selling. Ask the Assessor at 865-215-2360 how long the review will take before you set a closing date. Buyers' agents often pull the assessment history, so a record that matches the real house avoids questions late in the deal.

Years of nonpayment can lead to a tax sale handled through the Clerk and Master, where bidders must be current on their own taxes. The Trustee announces a sale date once the court sets one. An owner with delinquent years can have the balance paid from sale proceeds at closing, and a cash sale on a short timeline often suits an owner who is behind.

Gather these before you list: your latest tax notice, the parcel number, any exemption or relief paperwork, and a note of repairs or demolitions since January 1. The closing agent needs the first two, and the last two keep the bill accurate.

faqs.q: When are Knox County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by February 28 to avoid penalty and interest. Current-year taxes come due October 1, and a prior year's bill turns delinquent March 1.

faqs.q: What is the Knox County property tax rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the county levies $1.5540 per $100 of assessed value. If you live inside a city, add that city's rate, which you can get from the city.

faqs.q: Where does a Knox County owner file an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The county board comes first and starts meeting June 1. After that, the state board takes cases filed by August 1 or 45 days after the county notice went out. The Assessor at 865-215-2360 can arrange a field review before either step.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for the Knox County senior tax freeze?
faqs.a: The cutoff is April 5, 2027 for the 2026 tax year. You must reach age 65 by December 31, 2026, and 2025 combined income has to be under $63,470.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Knox County house that owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee gives a payoff figure and the closing agent takes it out of the seller's proceeds. Years of nonpayment can send an account to a court-run tax sale.
